name: Lever and static hold
pattern: Gymnastics static: straight arms hold the whole body still in a hard lever position (front lever, back lever, planche, L-sit, flag, cross), the trunk locked as one piece.
setup: Front lever: hang from a bar, hands shoulder width, palms away.
Pull your shoulders down and squeeze the bar; arms stay straight the whole time.
Start from the tuck version and only extend the legs when you can hold the tuck 10-15 seconds.

steps.text: Press the bar down toward your hips with straight arms until your body is level, face up, then hold still.

cues.why: These skills are judged and loaded as straight-arm holds; bent arms change the muscles and the skill.

cues.cue: Front lever: shoulders pulled down and back. Planche: shoulders pushed forward and down.
cues.why: The scapula sets each skill: depression and retraction for pulling holds, protraction with serratus for pushing holds; training drills that drop serratus work miss this.

cues.cue: Ribs down, glutes and legs squeezed, one straight line.
cues.why: A long, rigid body is needed for the lever; any sag adds a bending load the trunk cannot hold.

cues.cue: Move from tuck to advanced tuck to straddle to full.
cues.why: Body length and leg position set the lever arm; shorter shapes are much easier to hold.

cues.cue: Short holds, 5-15 seconds, several sets, fully rested.
cues.why: Static strength is trained near maximal effort; long fatigued holds break form.

breathing: Short, shallow breaths behind a braced trunk; do not hold your breath for long holds.

mistakes.name: Elbows bend
mistakes.looks: The elbows soften and the body sinks toward the bar or floor.
mistakes.fix: Lock the elbows and shorten the lever (tuck the knees) instead.
mistakes.why: Bending the arms turns the hold into a different, easier skill and loads the elbow.

mistakes.name: Hips drop or pike
mistakes.looks: In a front lever the hips sag below the line or bend up into a pike.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes, ribs down; go back to a tuck or straddle.
mistakes.why: Breaking at the hips shortens the lever to make it easier and hides weak spots.

mistakes.name: Shoulders collapse
mistakes.looks: The shoulders ride up to the ears in a lever, or sink and pinch back in a planche.
mistakes.fix: Lever: press the bar toward your hips. Planche: push the floor away and round the upper back slightly.
mistakes.why: Losing the scapular position moves the load from the muscles onto the shoulder joint.

safety: These are advanced skills: build pull-ups, dips and hollow holds first.
Straight-arm work loads the elbow and biceps tendon; add volume slowly over weeks.
Planche and lean holds load the wrists: warm them up and use parallettes if they hurt.
Iron cross and maltese place very high stress on the shoulder and elbow; do not attempt them without coaching.

variants.change: Knees pulled to the chest: much shorter lever.
Back flat, knees at about 90° to the trunk.
Legs straight and wide: shorter lever than the full version.
Moving version: lower slowly into the hold or raise up into it.
Lean planche: feet on the floor, shoulders far in front of the hands.
Frog or elbow planche: knees or hips rest on the bent elbows; a balance drill.
Hanging L-sit: hang from a bar with legs straight out at 90°.

subtypes.name: Front lever
subtypes.change: Hanging, body horizontal and face up, arms straight to the bar.

subtypes.name: Planche
subtypes.change: Hands on the floor or parallettes, body horizontal and face down, shoulders far ahead of the hands, feet off the floor.

subtypes.name: Back lever
subtypes.change: Hanging from a bar or rings, body horizontal and face down, arms straight behind the body.

subtypes.name: L-sit
subtypes.change: Hands on the floor or parallettes beside the hips, arms straight, hips lifted, legs straight out in front at about 90°.

subtypes.name: Dragon flag
subtypes.change: Lying face up on a bench, hands gripping behind the head; the body rises straight from the shoulders and lowers slowly as one plank, head lower than the feet.

subtypes.name: Human flag
subtypes.change: Gripping a vertical pole, top arm pulls and bottom arm pushes; the body sticks out sideways, level with the floor. The rig rolls the body 90° onto its side.

subtypes.name: Iron cross and maltese
subtypes.change: On rings, arms straight out to the sides. Cross: body upright, hands level with the shoulders. Maltese: body horizontal face down, hands at hip level.

motion.basis: Muscle roles (serratus, pectoralis, latissimus) from the ring-strength EMG studies bernasconi2004 and bernasconi2009, lever-arm and body-shape effects from wang2023 (planche model). Joint angles and scapular positions are our estimates from coaching texts (low2016); no kinematic study of these holds was found. The dragon flag trunk value (-135) means face up with the head lower than the feet.

sources.cite: Bernasconi S, Tordi N, Parratte B, Rouillon JD, Monnier G. Surface electromyography of nine shoulder muscles in two iron cross conditions in gymnastics. J Sports Med Phys Fitness. 2004;44(3):240-245.
